key_insight: A complete symmetry-invariant descriptor basis connects magnetic textures to response tensors through interpretable, hierarchically stable order parameters.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a systematic way to build physics-informed machine-learning models of response tensors in crystalline magnets.
method: Construct symmetry-invariant descriptors for arbitrary crystal structures and magnetic textures.
Modify principal component analysis to obtain uncorrelated order parameters that remain stable as higher spin orders are added.
Use the order parameters to regress and classify anomalous Hall conductivity in a magnetic kagome lattice.
evidence_signal: In the regime where linear regression models anomalous Hall conductivity well, ranked squared regression coefficients follow a Zipf-like power law; the abstract reports no numerical accuracy metrics.
watch_item: Validation is demonstrated on a magnetic kagome lattice, so predictive performance and computational cost for other crystal structures remain to be established.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Response Tensors in Crystalline Magnets: Application to Kagome Metals
